findings.done_when: the next three films' overview sheets show the named subject unoccluded and at least 150 px tall in 12 of 12 frames
findings.suggestion: Before a film renders, raycast from the camera to the subject on every keyframe and refuse occluded shots, the way the firefly test checks visibility. Frame the subject at 1/3 of the frame height, and write the overview sheet before posting, so a film that misses is never published.
findings.title: Films shot from inside a bush and at grass height: check every frame before posting
findings.what: magnet-stone-beach.mp4 spends 9 of 12 overview frames inside green foliage with tree trunks as silhouettes. compass-bowl.mp4 never shows the compass, only a bird's legs walking past a hydrangea. Both were posted.
findings.where: the movie pipeline / film camera placement; world/site posts for magnet stone and compass

findings.suggestion: If it is the ghost replay, give it a clear look of its own (translucent and blue-tinted, or a dotted outline) or remove it while the player is Lumi. If it is a chick, give it a different colour and name.

process: The author is productive but builds for themself: s145 to s148 went into electromagnetism solvers, soft-iron spike chains, paper-dart drag and wire benches. That is clever physics (goal 3 moves on paper), but a player sees grey boards and the films missed three times in one session, one posted without being looked at. The journal admits there was no player playthrough and no wish this session. Goal 1 (interactions) moves a little: toys in Jump in, and the key card is better. Goal 2 (a released film to be proud of): nothing since 2026-11-24, and #654 has been open for weeks. Goal 4 and goal 7 (rendering, a RayMakie showcase): stalled; the traced view looks like plastic noon with sky artefacts. Goal 5 (Lumi): mood words now show, but the yellow double and the dashboard contradictions undercut it. Goal 6 (animation and light): crab snaps and through-fence walking remain. Goal 8: ideas are original but always from the same physics-demo recipe, which the judge already punishes. Next sessions should check every film frame before posting, put creatures and real materials into one spectacular toy, and release a film.

animation.why: live_motion: 7 of 10 move well. Pinchy jumps 0.30 m in one frame and turns 93 degrees in one frame, Truffle's tail snaps 0.21 m, Lumi's beak jumps 0.15 m. The films open with a 0.07 to 0.12 jump at t=0.04 s (a first-frame pop in all three).

camera.why: magnet-stone-beach.mp4 is filmed from inside a tree's foliage, so most frames are flat green. compass-bowl.mp4 sits at grass height and never shows the bowl. In live follow mode a giant mushroom fills a third of the frame, and the firefly chase camera loses Lumi 37% of the time (failing test).

creatures.why: Crabs, pigs, sheep and Gloop are charming generated models. Lumi still walks with a smaller yellow chick double at its side (cam-follow.png, firefly-view-30s.png), Pinchy walks through the fence rails (motion/p148/motion.png), and the close-ups on the creatures sheet show mostly backs and rears.

fun.why: Jump in gained a floating magnet top and the key card now shows each toy's own keys, which is real progress. Firefly catch now fails its own tests: standing on a firefly doesn't catch it, and Lumi is blocked from view in 15 of 40 seconds. The toys are things to look at, not goals; there is still no reason to play twice.

lighting.why: Daytime raster is pleasant but lit by one sun with soft fill. The traced orbit still (p148/traced.png) is flat noon: no light of its own anywhere, grainy speckled clouds, and a row of black slabs floating above the sea. Night lamps and moon halo (#689, #636) were not improved this session.

materials.why: The copper wire bench in play is a pink stick on a dark grey slab (tests/shots/magnetstone-sweep.png). The traced island is all plastic and diffuse: the pond is a speckled light-blue disc, and there is no glass, metal, coat, sheen or subsurface you would notice. The hot-glass film was the only real attempt, and it is several posts back.

performance.why: frame median 4.4 ms, p95 8.6 ms, 30 fps steady; the path tracing toggle works.

props.why: Generated assets are everywhere: mushrooms, the TV, easels, hydrangeas. The physics toys are still primitives: slabs, rods, boxes.

style.why: Clay-toy creatures and props agree with each other. The physics benches (grey slab, raw rods) and the traced view's noisy clouds break the look.

ui.why: The key card fix helps. The dashboard still contradicts itself (Z sleeping icon over a 'meeting someone new' bubble, 'Pickles' and 'Lumi' labels stacked on one spot), and the right panel is a long wall of text.

world.why: Dense and varied up close, and the floating palm islets are a nice surprise in the raster view. They vanish in the traced view, though, and the island still reads as one round meadow crammed with props, with no areas that feel different.

wow.why: The last 20 posts are almost all small physics experiments with a caption, five of them misses. This session's three films show a bush interior, legs at grass height, and a tiny paper triangle. Nobody would forward any of them.

summary: In the raster view the island is a dense, cheerful toy box: generated creatures, floating palm islets in the sky, and a meadow full of flowers. The game around it still doesn't hold together. The follow camera loses Lumi behind mushrooms and trees, a small yellow chick double follows Lumi everywhere, and Lumi sleeps with a 'Z' over its head while its bubble says 'meeting someone new'. All three films from this session miss: the magnet-stone film is shot from inside a green bush, the compass film shows legs walking past a hydrangea, and the paper darts are a few pixels of grey triangle over raster-looking water. Session after session turns out clever physics on a board that nobody but the author can see.
